cases.evidence_note: Stage 19 mutation scenario, predicted by hand: blind return E1 with $500 of tax-free assistance received in 2026 for 2025 expenses (worksheet line 2b): line 27 $3,550 - $500 = $3,050, line 28 $1,050, line 29 $262.50, line 30 $2,262.50, line 7 $2,262.50 x 0.543 = $1,228.54.

Mutation scenario, predicted by hand: stage16.ira.i10 (single, aged 66, wages $20,000, Social Security benefits). The Social Security Benefits Worksheet copy of the IRA deduction limit is the smaller of the applicable amount ($7,000 plus the $1,000 catch-up at 50 or older, $8,000) and IRA Deduction Worksheet line 10 ($20,000 of compensation): $8,000 (i1040gi p. 98, line 12, "enter the smallest of line 7a, 10, or 11a").

stage21.refuse.limit_binds (a single filer born after January 1, 1961) read for Schedule 1-A Part V: no one on the return was born before January 2, 1961, so the count of seniors with a valid SSN and the count of a spouse who is one are both zero (p. 110).
